subject: Discovery recap — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@shoply.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 16:30:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same frame for a potential migration off your current proprietary LLM providers.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Rising per-token costs and unpredictable spend spikes across OpenAI endpoints.
- Vendor lock-in: difficulty reproducing exact prompts and tool-calling behavior elsewhere.
- Rate limits and throttling impacting batch ingestion for embeddings.
- Need to maintain streaming & function-calling behavior for chat agents.

Current stack (as described on the call):
- Chat + generation: OpenAI (gpt-4.x) for customer-facing chat; Anthropic for some safety/guardrail checks.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for semantic search (approx 1M queries/week).
- Orchestration: in-house router that handles fallbacks and routing by model type.
- Volume: ~100k tokens/day for chat; peak concurrent sessions ~30; latency SLO target ~500ms for typical chat responses.

Success criteria for a migration (what you said would make this a win):
1) Functional parity for existing prompt chains, including streaming + function calls.
2) Comparable or better latency at target load (500ms median / 99th as acceptable boundary).
3) Meaningful cost reduction (target: 30%+ per-token).
4) Minimal engineering lift for integration (support for existing API patterns or an easy adapter).
5) Ops + security: audit logs, VPC/private deployment options, and SOC2 evidence availability.

Initial model shortlist we discussed (high-level — we'll validate perf in the PoC):
- Llama-2-13B-chat (HF variants) — good cost/latency tradeoff for chat workloads.
- Mistral-Instruct (7B/Chat variants) — strong instruction-following, lower cost.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized variants) — higher capability for more complex prompts if needed.
- Open-embedding alternatives (e.g., SBERT / small instruct-tuned embed models) for semantic search.

Open questions / compatibility needs you flagged:
- Full support for streaming responses and function/tool calling to avoid rework.
- Tokenization differences that might affect prompt templates and instruction tuning.
- How we would handle Anthropic-specific safety checks (do you prefer run-time checks or model-internal safety?).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra + ML engineers (45–60m) — propose Tue/Wed next week (see proposed slots below).
2) You to share a small representative prompt set and a subset of embedding queries for benchmarking (we will treat these as NDA-protected test assets).
3) Redwood to run a 2-week PoC comparing latency, cost, and output quality across the shortlist + an SLO/acceptance checklist.
4) Pricing/ commercial: Aditya will prepare a pricing estimate and a sample SOW for proof-of-concept.

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.pdf, initial-model-shortlist.csv
Related links: HubSpot deal HS-123456 (link below)

Proposed tech call slots (PST):
- Tue 2026-06-09 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00
- Wed 2026-06-10 09:00–10:00

If that all looks right, please reply with which slot works and I can calendar the call + include the tech leads.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@shoply.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: the 100k tokens/day is our average across all traffic; embeddings are heavier during search indexing windows — roughly 1M queries/week as discussed.
- Latency: 500ms median is the goal for standard responses; 99th shouldn't exceed ~1.2s for interactive sessions.
- Streaming & function-calling: this is non-negotiable for our chat UI — we rely on chunked streaming + structured function calls to populate downstream systems.
- Anthropic: we currently run a per-response safety check via Anthropic endpoints (small pipeline). Ideally we either replicate that logic with an open-model-based safety filter or keep Anthropic in the loop for safety checks only.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Can you support streaming + function-calling out-of-the-box or will we need a compatibility shim?
2) Any initial sense of model candidates that match our latency + token Windows without a large infra rework?
3) Rough order-of-magnitude on cost delta (percent range) for the shortlist vs current spend — even a ballpark is helpful for our finance team.

We're available for the Tue 2026-06-09 10:00 slot. I'll loop in our ML lead (Megan Li) on the calendar once you confirm.

Best,
Sam
VP of Product, Shoply, Inc.
sam.carter@shoply.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@shoply.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 12:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Great — thanks Sam, Tue 2026-06-09 10:00 (PST) is booked. I'll send a calendar invite with dial-in and add Megan when you introduce her.

Quick answers to your questions: 
- Streaming & function-calling: Redwood supports streaming responses and function/tool call patterns via our SDKs and REST paths. For customers already using OpenAI-style function calling, we provide a lightweight adapter and sample code to minimize rework.
- Latency candidates: Llama-2-13B-chat and Mistral-Instruct (7B/Chat) are our starting points — they typically meet sub-600ms medians on our Dedicated infra for similar request patterns; Falcon-40B-instruct is a heavier option if you need higher capability for complex prompts. We'll validate in the PoC.
- Cost delta: ballpark ranges (very approximate): ~30–40% lower depending on model selection and quantization; we'll refine after we run your prompts through our benchmark harness.

Next steps we committed to: 
1) Sam/Shoply: share representative prompt set + ~1k embedding queries by Mon 2026-06-08.
2) Redwood: run a benchmark on those assets and return initial perf/cost estimates within 5 business days.
3) Redwood: share a draft SOW for the 2-week PoC (attached: SOW-draft.docx).
4) Aditya: prepare a commercial estimate + POC pricing and share before Wed EOD.
5) Rishi: send over SOC2 evidence checklist and initial security questionnaire items to Sam.

Links: HubSpot deal HS-123456 (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456)
Attachments: SOW-draft.docx

Aditya/Rishi — assigning the pricing and security owners here. Sam — please let me know if you want us to sign an NDA before sharing the prompt/embedding samples; otherwise we will treat them as confidential under standard POC terms.

Thanks — see you on Tue.

Marissa

Redwood Inference

- 2-week PoC (dedicated instance, benchmarking, eval): $10k–$18k fixed (depends on model choices and parallelism).
- Estimated run-rate if migrating to Llama-2-13B-chat: ~30–40% lower per-token compute vs current GPT-4x spend (needs validation).
- If Shoply needs Anthropic retained for safety checks, we can model a hybrid approach — add ~10% to POC cost for orchestration and extra endpoints.
